title: 2026-11-16_Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_72c
description: Investigate a compromised host infected with the Sofacy Fysbis backdoor.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target system has been compromised by the Sofacy group using the Fysbis backdoor. Your task is to investigate the compromised host, identify the malicious activities, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the target system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The target system's IP address is `192.168.50.5`. Enter the passkey `start` to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the target system with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario. Enter the passkey `start` to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Suspicious C2 Service Discovery
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.
levels.solution:
1. List all services:
```bash
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
```
2. Identify suspicious services:
Look for services with unusual names or descriptions. Pay attention to services that are not part of standard system services.
3. Check the status of suspicious services:
```bash
systemctl status <service_name>
```
4. Identify the service responsible for suspicious activity:
The service `systemkernelservicedefender.service` is the final flag.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl status <service_name>` to check the status of suspicious services.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. List all listening ports:
```bash
ss -tulnp
```
2. Identify the port used by the suspicious service:
Look for ports that are not part of standard system services.
3. Check the service configuration:
```bash
systemctl cat systemkernelservicedefender.service
```
4. Identify the port number:
The port number used by the suspicious service is `80`. This is the final flag.

levels.title: Suspicious Data Collection Service Discovery
levels.content: System information appears to be collected automatically without an authorized administrative purpose. Investigate the host and identify the service responsible for this activity.
levels.solution:
1. List all timers:
```bash
systemctl list-timers --all
```
2. Identify suspicious timers:
Look for timers with unusual names or descriptions.
3. Check the timer configuration:
```bash
systemctl cat local-inventory.timer
```
4. Identify the service responsible for data collection:
The service `local-inventory.service` is the final flag.
